assessment.nobel_worthiness: A clean, general mechanism: the Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model predicts that interlayer tunnelling in a small-angle bilayer flattens the bands near a magic angle, and experiment then found correlated insulators and superconductivity there. This is a theoretical idea that can be analysed and was tested sharply, which suits my taste. It opened the large field of moire quantum matter and gave a tunable platform for strongly correlated electrons.
assessment.attribution: Theory prediction (Bistritzer, MacDonald) and the 2018 experimental discovery (Jarillo-Herrero group) are the decisive pair. Eva Y. Andrei's earlier STM evidence of flat bands and Dean/Kim-type device contributions are real but secondary to the one-two punch of prediction plus transport discovery. A prize of theory-plus-experiment fits three names well.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced by many groups across several platforms within about seven years, and the flat-band picture is stable. Timing looks right; the pairing mechanism of the superconductivity remains open but that does not undercut the discovery itself.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is unresolved.
Whether Andrei's contribution deserves a place over Bistritzer is a judgement call among four credited names.
I am relying on memory for the details of who first measured what, not on any independent check.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The energy-landscape and funnel picture explains how a heteropolymer finds its native state despite an astronomically large conformation space, by using spin-glass ideas such as the random energy model and minimal frustration. It is statistical physics applied to a long-standing problem, and it is conceptually the sort of simple mechanism I value. It shaped the physical understanding of folding and later biomolecular simulation.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes brought the spin-glass and funnel framework and Onuchic the funnel and structure-based models, with long collaboration. Dill's work on hydrophobic collapse and lattice models is influential but a distinct line, and the Bryngelson-Wolynes 1987 paper is a root of the idea that is not fully captured in a three-name set.
assessment.maturity: Decades of experimental and computational support (folding kinetics, structure-based models), and the framework is widely taught. The recent chemistry prize for protein structure prediction does not overlap with this and may sharpen the contrast between prediction and understanding. Timing is fine, but a physics prize for biophysics is unusual.
uncertainties: Physics versus chemistry/biology boundary; the idea may be judged outside the physics prize's scope.
Credit split among Wolynes, Onuchic, Dill and early co-authors is uncertain.
Experimental confirmation is indirect and model-dependent.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Exact relations that hold arbitrarily far from equilibrium, including the Jarzynski equality and Crooks relation, extend the second law to fluctuations and let one extract equilibrium free energies from nonequilibrium work. This is a rigorous, universal result in the spirit of the physics I work on, and it is used in single-molecule experiments and stochastic thermodynamics.
assessment.attribution: Jarzynski (1997) and Evans with Cohen and Morriss (1993) are the key origins. Crooks formulated the detailed fluctuation relation in 1999. Gallavotti-Cohen and Searles belong to this story but are not in the credited names, so the attribution is awkward and the three-name set is incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally verified in RNA-unfolding and other single-molecule experiments and in colloidal and electrical systems. It has been mature for about twenty years. Recognition is not premature.
uncertainties: Attribution is contested because Gallavotti, Cohen and Searles are not in the credited list.
Whether the Committee views this as a discovery of sufficient scope remains unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Halperin-Nelson-Young theory predicts that two-dimensional melting proceeds via two continuous transitions with an intermediate hexatic phase, by unbinding of dislocations and then disclinations. It is a clear and elegant statistical-physics mechanism, closely related to the topological defect ideas recognised in 2016.
assessment.attribution: Halperin and Nelson (1978) and Young (1979) are the decisive theory papers, and three names fit well. Kosterlitz and Thouless already have the Nobel, so the attribution here is clean. Experimental observation of the hexatic in colloids and liquid crystals came from other groups not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Many decades old with solid experimental verification in colloidal and other systems. Some simulation work shows first-order melting in certain systems, so the universal scenario has qualifications. Late but not premature.
uncertainties: Whether the 2016 prize makes this redundant in the Committee's eyes.
Simulations show system-dependent melting scenarios.
Experimental credit is outside the listed names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators connect band-structure topology to protected edge and surface states, with the quantum spin Hall effect predicted by Kane and Mele and the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal observed in HgTe, followed by quantum anomalous Hall in magnetic films. The concepts are general and have shaped the field.
assessment.attribution: A compound discovery. Kane and Mele (with Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, not credited here) for theory, Molenkamp for the experimental quantum spin Hall effect and Xue for the quantum anomalous Hall effect. Hasan is credited elsewhere on the longlist and the omission of Mele, Zhang and Hasan is a real fairness problem.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by many groups, ARPES and transport. The prize question is mostly about credit, not maturity. Timing is good.
uncertainties: Credit allocation is the main problem: Zhang, Mele, Hasan, Moore and others are all arguably decisive.
The three-name set mixes theory with two different experiments.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory turns the lattice problem of strongly correlated electrons into an impurity problem that becomes exact in infinite dimensions. It is a controlled, mean-field-like idea of the sort I find convincing, and it gave the first unified description of the Mott transition and, through DFT+DMFT, quantitative methods for correlated materials.
assessment.attribution: Metzner and Vollhardt introduced the infinite-dimensional limit, Georges and Kotliar built the mapping onto an impurity model, and Müller-Hartmann also contributed to it. Three names are reasonable but the allocation among these early contributors is not obvious.
assessment.maturity: Well established and widely used for about thirty years. Its value rests on theory validated against materials data rather than one decisive experiment.
uncertainties: Metzner and Müller-Hartmann's role in the original limit is not captured in the credited names.
Accuracy for real materials is limited by the impurity solver and the lack of nonlocal correlations.
A theoretical method may fit a prize less naturally than a discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Leinaas and Myrheim showed that identical particles in two dimensions admit fractional statistics, and later experiments detected fractional charge and anyonic statistics. This is a deep and general idea about quantum statistics, and its recent experimental confirmation is striking.
assessment.attribution: Leinaas and Myrheim (1977) for the original theory, with Wilczek, Halperin and Arovas-Schrieffer-Wilczek also central but absent from the credited list. Heiblum led the fractional charge shot-noise measurements. Fève and Manfra lead the recent braiding results, so the experimental credit is divided.
assessment.maturity: Fractional charge is well confirmed. The anyon braiding experiments in interferometers and collider geometries are recent, with some interpretational debate. I judge the experimental half to be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Wilczek and Halperin are missing from the credited names.
Interpretation of the anyon interferometry experiments is still being checked.
Allocation across theory and several experimental groups is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise the Hubbard model and related many-body systems with tunable parameters, and the superfluid-to-Mott transition observed in 2002 made quantum simulation practical. It links directly to statistical mechanics, giving a clean controllable laboratory for ideas I know from theory.
assessment.attribution: Jaksch, Zoller and colleagues proposed the Bose-Hubbard realisation, Greiner (with Bloch and Hänsch) observed the Mott transition, and Esslinger demonstrated the fermionic Mott insulator. Cirac is credited but more central to the trapped-ion and general quantum-simulation proposals. A three-name set leaves out Esslinger and Jaksch.
assessment.maturity: The field is mature, with quantum gas microscopes and many replicated results. Some recognition has already come through earlier cold-atom prizes, so overlap with those could count against it.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2001 BEC prize and earlier atomic physics prizes.
Many comparably strong contributors for a three-person limit.
Whether quantum simulation has delivered decisive new physics rather than benchmarks.
